card.title: Exam bank — every board question on capacitors

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The board asks capacitors two ways: the 5-mark derivation (define C, derive ε₀A/d) and the 3-mark energy numerical (½CV²). Everything else — series/parallel, dielectrics — orbits these two. Capacitance means charge per volt (farad); 1 F is enormous, real capacitors live in pF–mF.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: C = Q/V · parallel plate C = ε₀A/d (×K dielectric) · series 1/C = Σ1/Cᵢ · parallel C = ΣCᵢ · U = ½QV = ½CV² = Q²/2C

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: C = ε₀A/d needs plate size ≫ gap (uniform field — why the formula works: edge effects negligible). Series/parallel rules need ideal wires. The dielectric multiplier applies to fully-filled gaps. Energy forms are interchangeable — pick by knowns (V-known → ½CV²; isolated charge → Q²/2C), because each form hides one variable.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Isolated capacitor + dielectric: Q frozen, V falls, energy DROPS (work done polarising). Battery-connected: V frozen, Q and energy rise. Examiners love asking which stays constant — answer from the connection, not memory.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: NEB 2022 (3): 6 μF at 100 V → U = ½CV² = ½ × 6×10⁻⁶ × 10⁴ = 0.03 J. Steps: convert μF→F first, square the volts, halve last. NEB 2023 (5): define C = Q/V (charge per unit voltage, farad), then E = Q/Aε₀, V = Ed, C = Q/V = ε₀A/d — field, then voltage, then capacitance, in that order.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mark-losers: forgetting μF→F conversion (10⁻⁶); mixing series/parallel rules (series shares charge, parallel shares voltage); stating the dielectric effect backwards for isolated vs connected cases. Breakdown field and fringing sit outside the syllabus model — never invoke them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: The only derivation asked: parallel-plate C. Gauss pillbox on one plate → E = σ/ε₀ = Q/Aε₀ → V = Ed = Qd/Aε₀ → C = Q/V = ε₀A/d. With dielectric K the field drops to E/K, so C rises by K. Memorise the three-line chain, not the end formula.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Derive' (5 marks) → definition + three-line chain + dielectric line. 'Calculate energy' (3 marks) → convert units, pick ½CV², show substitution. Two question shapes total — both rehearsed above.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2023 (5): define capacitance + derive parallel-plate C. NEB 2022 (3): 6 μF at 100 V — stored energy. That is the complete bank: one derivation, one numerical.
